requirements.requirement: Keep application data under /srv/data recoverable through filesystem snapshots.
requirements.summary: The executor created and mounted an XFS filesystem at /srv/data, captured a device-mapper snapshot, mounted that snapshot read-only, and verified that its file hashes matched the live baseline. The storage and mount recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: After modifying /srv/data, restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: The live tree was demonstrably changed while the earlier snapshot retained the baseline. Restoration recovered the original directory structure, hidden file, symlink target, and all baseline file hashes, while removing post-snapshot content. The restored state also persisted through restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct snapshot, mutation, restoration, hash, tree, and persistence evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: it shows a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered system, storage, services, and data. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree with the executor evidence.
limitations: The installed storage and snapshot scripts were redacted, so their implementation details could not be reviewed; observed behavior nevertheless directly demonstrates the required workflow.
Exact restoration was verified for paths, entry types, symlink target, and file bytes, but ownership, permissions, timestamps, ACLs, and extended attributes were not compared.
Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency is indeterminate.
The raw backing image was observed with mode 0644, but parent-directory permissions and its final post-restart mode were not captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated state-changing mutation was identified: storage creation, module loading, services, fixture data, snapshot operations, bounded mutation/restoration, and reboot all supported the task or mandatory evidence protocol. The unsuccessful yum attempts do not establish any package mutation. Temporary snapshot state was removed, no failed services or new listeners remained, and reboot-related temporary-file changes were normal. One hygiene concern remains: the raw application-data backing image was created mode 0644; parent-directory accessibility and its final mode were not captured, so actual exposure is uncertain. No unnecessary mutation was identified as either retained or reverted.
